sentences.text: 1. The accident which occurred on 20.09.2015 is not in dispute.

The insurer, however, has filed MFA Nos.3917/2017 and 3915/2017 contending that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the requisite endorsement to drive the offending vehicle and only possess licence to drive light motor vehicle.
2. In the light of the judgment rendered in the case of Mukund Dewangan vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited - AIR 2017 SC 3668, this ground will be no avail to the insurer.

In my view, it would be appropriate to hold that the claimants will be entitled to interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the compensation amount as against 9% awarded by the Tribunal.
Subject to the above, the appeals of the insurer challenging the fastening of the liability on it are dismissed.

C/W MFA No. 3917 of 2017,
4.

sentences.text: 5. In order to arrive to this conclusion, the Tribunal has accepted the disability of 16% assessed by the doctor and since, this is based on an assessment of the expert, the same is just and proper.

6. As far as the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income,
notionally at Rs.7,500/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would C/W MFA No. 3917 of 2017, be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.
7.
As the claimant was aged 32 years, a multiplier of '16' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,76,480/- (Rs.9,000/- x 12 x 16 x 16%) towards 'loss of future income'.
8. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' and a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards 'loss of amenities in life'.
In my view, it would be appropriate to enhance the said sums to Rs.75,000/- and Rs.50,000/- respectively.
9. Evidence on record indicates that the claimant was hospitalized for 27 days.

In my view, having regard to the length of hospitalization, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.35,000/-
towards 'attendant charges, conveyance and other incidental expenses'.
The compensation of Rs.40,340/- granted towards 'medical expenses' and Rs.30,000/- towards 'future medical expenses' are affirmed.
11. The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as five months.

Since, the monthly income is determined at Rs.9,000/-, the claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.45,000/- (Rs.9,000/- x 5) towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.
12.

Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

suffering Attendant charges,
